title: Advanced ChatGPT
description: ChatGPT is more than a chat window. This lesson shows you three advanced capabilities that turn ChatGPT into a production tool: Custom GPTs, Code Interpreter, and the API.
learningObjectives: Create a Custom GPT for a specific task
Use Code Interpreter to analyze data and files
Understand how the API enables integration with your own applications
Design workflows that combine ChatGPT with other tools

opening.hook: Most people use ChatGPT as a chat window — ask a question, get an answer. But ChatGPT can do much more: analyze your data, create custom tools, and integrate with your own software. This lesson shows you how.
opening.relevance: These capabilities are the difference between using ChatGPT casually and building with ChatGPT professionally.

content.content: Custom GPTs let you configure ChatGPT for specific tasks with preset instructions, knowledge files, and tools. They are shareable and reusable — a way to package expertise into a tool.

content.definition: A configured version of ChatGPT with custom instructions, knowledge, and capabilities.
content.example: A 'Legal Contract Reviewer' Custom GPT with templates and legal guidelines baked in.

content.title: How to build a Custom GPT
steps: 1. Name and describe the GPT — e.g., 'Code Reviewer'
2. Set instructions: 'You review Python code for style, correctness, and security.'
3. Upload knowledge files: code style guides, examples
4. Configure capabilities: enable code execution if needed

content.title: When to use a Custom GPT
content.content: Use Custom GPTs when you repeat the same task frequently, when you need consistent output style, or when you want to share expertise with others.
ChatGPT can execute Python code in a sandboxed environment. This allows it to analyze data, generate charts, and work with files — tasks that a text-only model could not do.

content.definition: A ChatGPT capability that runs Python code to analyze data, generate visualizations, and process files.
content.example: Upload a CSV of sales data — ChatGPT can compute totals, generate charts, and find trends.

content.title: What Code Interpreter can do:
items: Run Python code (pandas, matplotlib, numpy, etc.)

content.title: Data analysis workflow
steps: Upload: 'sales_data.csv' with columns: date, product, revenue
Prompt: 'Analyze this data. Show monthly revenue trends and identify top products.'
ChatGPT: Writes Python code, runs it, returns charts and insights.

content.title: Practical limitations
items: Code Interpreter cannot access the internet
Files are temporary — you cannot store data persistently
Complex workflows may need to be broken into steps

content.content: The OpenAI API lets you integrate ChatGPT into your own applications. This is how businesses build custom AI tools, chatbots, and automation — without requiring users to open ChatGPT in a browser.

content.definition: A way for software to talk to ChatGPT programmatically.
content.example: A company uses the API to auto-summarize incoming support tickets.

content.title: What you can build with the API:
items: Custom chatbots integrated into your website
AI-powered search on your own data

content.title: Automation workflow
steps: 1. Incoming email arrives in your inbox
2. Zapier detects the email and calls the API
3. ChatGPT summarizes the email and drafts a reply
4. Zapier sends the draft to you for review
5. You approve — Zapier sends the final reply

content.title: Cost and control
content.content: APIs charge by usage (per token). This means you pay for what you use — but you also need to monitor costs and set rate limits. Control matters when you integrate AI into production systems.

content.myth: APIs are only for developers at big companies.
content.reality: Tools like Zapier and Make let non-developers connect ChatGPT to workflows without writing code.

keyTakeaways: Custom GPTs let you package expertise into reusable tools.
Code Interpreter turns ChatGPT into a data analyst.
The API enables integration with your own applications.
Automation tools (Zapier, Make) make API workflows accessible without code.

reflection.prompt: Which of these three capabilities (Custom GPTs, Code Interpreter, API) is most relevant to your work or study?
reflection.hint: Custom GPTs for consistent tasks, Code Interpreter for data, API for automation.
reflection.expectedInsight: The advanced capabilities of ChatGPT are not about better answers — they are about new workflows.

flashcards.back: A configured ChatGPT with custom instructions, knowledge, and capabilities.
Execute Python code, analyze files, generate charts, process data.
To integrate ChatGPT into your own applications for custom AI workflows.

flashcards.front: What is a limitation of Code Interpreter?
flashcards.back: Cannot access the internet. Files are temporary.
Yes — tools like Zapier and Make let you connect ChatGPT to workflows without code.

items.question: You want ChatGPT to always respond in the same style for a specific task. What should you use?
items.explanation: A Custom GPT lets you define permanent instructions and behavior for a specific task.
items.whyItMatters: Custom GPTs solve the 'consistent output' problem.

items.question: You have a spreadsheet with sales data and want ChatGPT to analyze it. What do you use?
options: Code Interpreter — upload the file and ask ChatGPT to analyze it
items.explanation: Code Interpreter is designed for data analysis. Upload the file, ask for analysis, and ChatGPT writes and runs Python code.
items.whyItMatters: This capability turns ChatGPT into a data analyst.

items.question: Describe a workflow that combines Custom GPT + API + automation tool.
items.answer: Example: A 'Support Ticket Classifier' Custom GPT with API access — Zapier calls the API for each incoming ticket, gets the classification, and routes it to the right team.
items.explanation: Combining all three enables end-to-end automation. The Custom GPT defines the task; the API enables access; automation tools orchestrate the workflow.
items.whyItMatters: This is the highest-level use of ChatGPT — building production systems.

items.question: Your company receives 500 support tickets per day. You want to categorize them automatically. What approach would you take?
items.answer: Use the ChatGPT API with a few-shot prompt that includes examples of each category. Optionally, build a Custom GPT with the categorization instructions, then call the API from a script or automation tool to process each ticket.
items.explanation: This combines several techniques: few-shot prompting for consistency, structured output for automation, and the API for scaling.
items.whyItMatters: This is a realistic example of turning ChatGPT into a production tool.

notes.summary: ChatGPT's advanced capabilities: Custom GPTs (reusable tools), Code Interpreter (data analysis), and API (integration). Combine them to build workflows.
keyPoints: Custom GPTs = configured ChatGPT for specific tasks
Code Interpreter = Python execution for data analysis
Automation tools connect everything without code

importantTerms.definition: Zapier, Make, etc. — connect apps without code.

notes.reflection: Advanced ChatGPT is about workflows, not just better answers.
